title: Is Trash Evolving Raccoons Into the Next Household Pet?
titleZh: 驯化的浣熊，城市新宠物？
summary:
随着人类活动持续向自然领域扩张，一种全新的家养宠物或许正在悄然诞生，一种越来越适应我们所建造的城市空间的动物。阿肯色大学小石城分校的研究人员此前注意到，浣熊的解剖结构正在发生变化，并开始思考小浣熊（网友昵称为little trash pandas）是否仅因长期生活在人类身边，便正在经历某种驯化过程。研究人员在《动物学前沿》期刊上发表的研究指出，与乡村地区的浣熊相比，城市浣熊的吻部更短，这一变化与许多已被驯化物种的特征演变相似。基于这一发现，或许在不远的将来，我们真的能够将又一个物种带进家中，近距离感受它们的温顺与探索欲，而不再只是远远观望。

来源：Discover；作者：Jenny Lehmann；原文发布时间：2025-11-16 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Humans’ ongoing expansion into natural environments might be triggering the evolution of a new household pet, one that’s increasingly comfortable in the urban spaces we create. Researchers from the University of Arkansas at Little Rock (UALR) noticed anatomical changes in raccoons and wondered whether these little trash pandas are actually undergoing a domestication process simply by spending so much time around us. Their study, published in Frontiers of Zoology, describes how urban raccoons have smaller snouts compared to their rural counterparts, similar to patterns seen in other domesticated species. Based on this discovery, we might one day welcome another species into our homes, enjoying their tameness and curiosity not just from a distance.
paragraphs.contentZh: 随着人类活动持续向自然领域扩张，一种全新的家养宠物或许正在悄然诞生，一种越来越适应我们所建造的城市空间的动物。阿肯色大学小石城分校的研究人员此前注意到，浣熊的解剖结构正在发生变化，并开始思考小浣熊（网友昵称为little trash pandas）是否仅因长期生活在人类身边，便正在经历某种驯化过程。研究人员在《动物学前沿》期刊上发表的研究指出，与乡村地区的浣熊相比，城市浣熊的吻部更短，这一变化与许多已被驯化物种的特征演变相似。基于这一发现，或许在不远的将来，我们真的能够将又一个物种带进家中，近距离感受它们的温顺与探索欲，而不再只是远远观望。

paragraphs.contentEn: To investigate whether urban environments alone could start the domestication process in previously undomesticated animals, the research group focused on raccoons, which are an ideal species thanks to their widespread rural and urban populations. They analyzed nearly 20,000 images of raccoons from across the continental U.S., provided by citizen scientists and collected through iNaturalist.org.
paragraphs.contentZh: 为了探究仅凭城市环境本身是否就足以推动原本未被驯化动物的驯化进程，研究团队选择了浣熊这一理想研究对象，因为它们在美国城乡地区都分布广泛。研究人员依托iNaturalist.org平台，分析了美国本土各地公民科学家上传的近2万张浣熊影像。

paragraphs.contentEn: A clear difference emerged between raccoons avoiding human environments and those thriving in metropolitan areas. Like dogs, urban raccoons displayed shorter snouts, likely because tamer individuals are better tolerated by humans and more successful in cities. What draws them closer to our dwellings in the first place, however, is our abundant and easily accessible garbage. “Trash is really the kickstarter,” said senior study author Raffaela Lesch, assistant professor of biology at the UALR, in a news statement. “Wherever humans go, there is trash. Animals love our trash. It’s an easy source of food. All they have to do is endure our presence, not be aggressive, and then they can feast on anything we throw away.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究人员发现，那些避开人类活动的浣熊与在大城市中繁衍良好的浣熊之间，存在显著差异。与狗的特征变化相似，城市浣熊的吻部更短，这可能是因为性情更温顺的个体更容易被人类容忍，因此更容易在城市环境中生存。但最初吸引它们靠近人类聚集区的，仍然是我们产生的大量且易于获取的垃圾。该研究的资深作者、UALR生物学助理教授拉斐拉·莱施在新闻声明中表示：“垃圾才是整个过程的启动器。人类所到之处，总会留下垃圾。动物天然喜欢我们的垃圾。因为那是现成的食物来源。它们只需要学会容忍我们的存在、不表现攻击性，就能享用人类丢弃的一切。”

paragraphs.contentEn: The research team notes in their study that many people think of domestication as a purely human-driven, “unnatural” process. But animals can also adapt to human environments on their own by seeking abundant resources and safety from predators. Over time, these conditions can lead to traits associated with domestication even without direct human involvement.
paragraphs.contentZh: 研究团队在论文中指出，许多人将驯化视为一种完全由人类推动的“非自然”过程。但动物其实也会为了获取充足食物和躲避天敌，主动适应人类环境。随着时间推移，即便没有人类的直接干预，这些条件同样可能促使它们逐渐演化出与驯化相关的特征。

paragraphs.contentEn: To thrive in this new niche, animals benefit from adapting to harmonize with humans, appearing tamer and less fearful. The researchers argue that these early stages of domestication are driven entirely by natural selection. Their observations align with the Neural Crest Domestication Syndrome (NCDS) hypothesis, which suggests that animals undergoing domestication show similar anatomical and morphological changes that begin early in embryonic development. These shifts often appear as smaller skulls, floppy ears, pigmentation changes, and curly tails.
paragraphs.contentZh: 如果想在这一新兴生态位中生存并发展，动物需要通过适应自身行为，以更好地融入人类环境，表现得更温顺、也更少恐惧人类。研究人员指出，驯化的早期阶段完全由自然选择驱动。他们的观察结果也与神经嵴驯化综合征（NCDS）假说相一致，该假说认为，正在经历驯化的动物在胚胎发育早期便会出现一系列相似的解剖和形态变化。这些变化通常表现为头骨缩小、耳朵下垂、色素分布改变以及尾巴卷曲等。

paragraphs.contentEn: This project was largely driven by 16 students under the supervision of their biology professor, who wanted to make her biometry class more engaging. “I wanted to teach this class in a way that students would have their own data that they collect and analyze,” Lesch said. “The benefit is that I didn’t have to push students to complete the work. They were intrinsically motivated because they cared.” Their work ultimately proved strong enough to be published in a high-quality, peer-reviewed journal, an impressive achievement for young researchers and a great jump-start to their scientific careers.
paragraphs.contentZh: 这项研究主要由16名学生在一位生物学教授的指导下完成，而这位教授的初衷只是想提升自己生物统计学课程的吸引力。莱施表示：“我想用一种全新的方式授课，让学生能够亲自收集并分析属于他们自己的数据。这样做的好处在于，我完全不需要督促他们。他们有内在动力，因为他们在乎自己研究的内容。”最终，这项学生主导的研究质量足够扎实，被一家高水平的同行评审期刊接收发表，对于这些年轻研究者而言，这是一项相当亮眼的成就，也为他们的科研之路赢得了一个出色的开端。

paragraphs.contentEn: Next, the team hopes to repeat their study with other urban mammals, such as armadillos and opossums, to test whether similar domestication patterns appear across species. Still, their findings on raccoons highlight how humans’ presence alone can act as a driver of evolution, and who knows, may eventually bring us a brand-new pet. Lesch added, “It would be fitting and funny if our next domesticated species [were] raccoons. I feel like it would be funny if we called the domesticated version of the raccoon the trash panda.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 接下来，研究团队计划将同样的方法应用到其他城市哺乳动物身上，例如犰狳和负鼠，以检验类似的驯化模式是否会在不同物种间出现。但无论结果如何，他们对浣熊的研究已经表明，仅仅是人类的存在本身，就足以成为推动动物进化的力量；而且谁知道呢，这或许最终会为我们带来一种全新的家养宠物。莱施补充说：“如果下一个被驯化的物种真的是浣熊，那可谓既贴切又好笑。我甚至觉得，如果我们把驯化后的浣熊称作小垃熊（the trash panda），那就再合适不过了。”
